title: Pricing messaging framework — metrics, token rationale, tiers & discounts
content:
Purpose:
Draft guidance for public-facing messaging, sales scripts, and internal positioning on metric framing (why tokens), tier design, and discount language. Goal: make pricing simple to understand, defensible against competitors, and aligned with product levers (latency, quality, caching, dedicated capacity).

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
We recommend token-based billing as the primary metric because it aligns cost to usage granularity, incentivizes customers to optimize prompts, and maps directly to our serving resource units. Public messaging should start with simple, customer-centric anchors (cost per 1k tokens, typical session examples) then offer transparent paths to predictability: monthly committed capacity (Reserved), per-seat or per-route add-ons for routing/SLAs, and enterprise Private licensing. Discounting should be framed as volume and commitment rewards (not arbitrary coupons): predictable discounts for committed monthly/annual spend, higher discounts for dedicated capacity purchases, and usage thresholds that unlock progressive discounts.

Why tokens? (short bullets for marketing + sales):
- Direct correlation to compute work: tokens = model steps. Easier to explain than opaque GPU-hour pricing.
- Allows micro-billing for bursty, PLG usage and experimental dev flows.
- Encourages healthy user behavior (prompt engineering, caching) because customers see cost impact linearly.
- Fairness across model sizes: unitization by token is model-agnostic if we show normalized cost-per-token by model class (e.g., base, L, XL).

Potential customer objections and rebuttals (sales playbook snippets):
- "Why not charge per request?" -> "Per-request hides variability: a single request can be 20 tokens or 20k tokens. Token pricing ties cost to output length and compute. We show typical session examples so you can estimate monthly spend."
- "GPU-hour would be simpler for enterprise." -> "GPU-hour is great for capacity planning but not for developer experimentation. We offer Reserved capacity & dedicated pools for predictable GPU economics for teams that prefer it."
- "Won't token pricing reward long-winded outputs?" -> "We surface output quality metrics and recommend structured output/function-calls to keep responses concise. Also provide quantization, caching, and batching guidance to reduce cost-per-token without losing quality."

Metric framing guidance (website copy + pricing page):
- Lead with a consumer-friendly unit: cost per 1,000 tokens (USD / 1k tokens). Show 3 quick examples: short chat reply (~50 tokens), standard answer (~350 tokens), long summary (~2,000 tokens) with corresponding micro-costs.
- Provide a calculator widget: paste sample prompts or expected monthly queries to estimate spend.
- For advanced pages: show normalized cost-per-output = cost-per-1k-tokens * avg_tokens_per_output for typical workloads (chat, retrieval-augmented, embed-heavy).

Tier design recommendations (naming + what to include):
- Free / Starter: tight rate limits, low free token allotment, great for onboarding and PLG virality.
- Growth: usage-based token pricing, basic SLA, access to standard models, self-serve analytics.
- Scale: committed monthly spend discount, dedicated concurrency lanes, longer retention in Console, rollout controls.
- Dedicated / Enterprise: Reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual), enhanced SLAs, Private deploy options, white-glove onboarding and cost review.
Note: emphasize same API surface across tiers; call out which features are additive vs. gated by tier.

Discounting language & guardrails (public site + sales):
- Public page: present simple percent-off tiers for committed spend (e.g., 10% at $X/month, 20% at $Y/month). Keep language: "Volume discounts for committed usage" and avoid one-off or time-limited sounding "coupons" on high-touch enterprise pages.
- For sales: discounts are primarily a function of commitment horizon (monthly vs annual) and capacity mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Example guidance: up to 15% for monthly commitments above threshold A; up to 30% for 12-month commitments above threshold B; additional bespoke discounts reserved for multi-year/large enterprise buys.
- Anti-erosion rules: discounting must be tied to verifiable metrics (committed spend, reserved GPU units, seat counts). Avoid ad-hoc percentage concessions without corresponding contractual commitments.

Competitive analysis snapshot (how competitors price, what customers care about):
- Provider A (per-request): simple UX but poor for variable-length outputs — customers complain about unpredictability for long outputs.
- Provider B (per-concurrent-hour): predictable for high-throughput infra teams; less attractive to PLG.
- Provider C (token-based, but opaque tiers): many customers choose it for predictability but later complain about buried surcharges (e.g., for function-calls, tool-usage).
Positioning opportunity: market the combination — token granularity for developer experience + committed reserved options for enterprise predictability. Emphasize transparent line items (model class multipliers, function-call add-on).

Sales tactics and examples (one-liners + email snippets):
- Cold/email opener: "Estimate your current model spend in 2 minutes — paste a sample session and we'll show cost per 1k tokens and suggested reserved plan."
- Closing language: "Sign a 12-month reservation and lock in up to X% discount plus predictable throughput and a dedicated lane for peak traffic."
- Negotiation anchor: always anchor to TCO: show monthly spend projection across our tier vs competitor (tokens vs GPU-hour) on 3 workload shapes.

Examples & worked numbers (for internal use only):
- Example workload: 5k monthly sessions, avg 400 tokens -> 2M tokens/month. At $0.6 per 1k tokens = $1,200/month. 12-month reservation at 15% = $1,020/month.
- Example enterprise: 1B tokens/month -> negotiate Dedicated Reserved; show per-token blended price, expected 25–40% savings vs on-demand.

UX & Console notes (to product):
- Show live cost meter on API key dashboard with projected monthly spend and tipping points where a reserved tier would be cheaper.
- Provide automated suggestions: "Based on last 30 days, reserve X tokens/month to save Y%" with quick checkout.
- Add visibility for per-route costs and per-model cost multipliers so teams can optimize.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Public vs enterprise disclosure of model multipliers (should we display model size-adjusted per-token multipliers publicly?).
- Bundled seat vs token economics for hybrid workflows (where product teams want seat-based pricing for developer environments but token billing for production).
- How to price function-calls or tool-invocations cleanly — add-on token surcharge or baked into model token counts?

Next steps (short checklist):
- Finalize sample cost table for pricing page (3 model classes + session examples) — owner: Leila (due 2026-03-10).
- Mockup UI copy & cost-savings suggestion in Console — owner: Marc (due 2026-03-18).
- Decide public disclosure policy for model multipliers — GTM + Product sync (meeting 2026-03-05).

Notes to self (rough brainstorm fragments):
- Consider a "predictor" that maps product metrics (monthly MAU, avg tokens/session) -> recommended committed bucket.
- Could introduce a "token credits" UX that behaves like cents in a wallet; easier to reason about for finance teams.
- Keep discounting simple and formulaic: percentage by commitment length and volume band.
